title: The Places That Help
synopsis: Travel north through a landscape of people transformed into places, and decide how to answer their requests.

the_bridge.text: On the road north, you meet Mara, a woman who became a bridge during a flood so her brother could cross. He did, but travelers kept needing her, and the river has slowly worn her down. She asks whether the pear trees at Bell Orchard are still standing; the question sounds like a way to ask whether anyone remembers who she was before she became useful.

choices.text: Tell Mara the orchard still has three pear trees
Ask what she remembers of being human

the_spring.text: Beyond the bridge, a man has become a spring. Stones are caught in his mouth, slowing the water. He asks you to clear them. In return, he can tell you which mountain path is still open. Water is gathering in the fields below; your choice will cost either his relief or your time.

choices.text: Clear the stones from the spring
Ask for the route first; you need to reach Bell before night

the_ash_tree.text: An ash tree asks you to carry three seeds to the valley, where the soil is softer. Birds nest in the woman's hair. She has forgotten the sound of her own voice, but remembers the shade her branches make at noon. She does not ask you to stay; she asks whether you will remember her after you leave.

choices.text: Take the seeds and promise to plant them
Stay until evening and listen to the birds in her branches

text.value: At Bell, an old man recognizes Mara's name. She is his aunt, long believed dead. He wants to leave for the bridge at once; his granddaughter persuades him to pack food and hire a cart.
At Bell, you tell an old man what Mara remembers of the orchard. He knows her as the aunt his family lost. His granddaughter brings a cart and asks you to show her the road back to the river.

choices.text: Plant the ash seeds beside the orchard wall before leaving
Leave without planting; you did not take the seeds
Take the cart straight back so Mara's family can reunite

text.value: Mara recognizes her nephew's voice before he reaches the river. They sit on opposite banks and trade news. Behind you, the spring runs freely; the man can speak without stones in his mouth. You can stay for the reunion or continue north.

Mara recognizes her nephew's voice before he reaches the river. They sit on opposite banks and trade news. Behind you, the spring's water still gathers against the stones; the route got you here sooner, but the valley will flood if no one returns to help. You can stay for the reunion or continue north.

choices.text: Stay and help travelers clear the branches caught beneath Mara
Continue north, carrying the stories of the people you met

text.value: Travelers cross while Mara and her family speak across the water. The ash seeds are under the orchard wall, where someone will have to water them through the dry weeks. When evening comes, her granddaughter promises to return with food and news. The bridge remains a person, a place, and a choice the community keeps making together.

Travelers cross while Mara and her family speak across the water. You kept the seeds in your pocket; tending the reunion meant leaving the valley's future for another day. Her granddaughter promises to return with food and news. The bridge remains a person, a place, and a choice the community keeps making together.

Travelers cross while Mara and her family speak across the water. The ash tree remains behind without its seeds, but the birds have one more evening in her branches. Her granddaughter promises to return with food and news. The bridge remains a person, a place, and a choice the community keeps making together.

You walk north with empty pockets and the knowledge that three seeds are under the orchard wall, where someone must care for them next. Somewhere behind you, a bridge hears her family laugh. Ahead, the road bends out of sight.

You walk north with three seeds in your pocket and the reunion's last words still with you. The valley will have to wait. Somewhere behind you, a bridge hears her family laugh. Ahead, the road bends out of sight.
You walk north with the sound of birds in your memory and no seeds in your pocket. Somewhere behind you, a bridge hears her family laugh. Ahead, the road bends out of sight.
